definition: A diagnostic interview is a clinician-administered assessment used to determine whether a person meets the diagnosis for a particular mental disorder. In this context, it serves as a reference method against which self-report screening measures can be compared.

reasons: The packet states that PNI/NPI were evaluated for convergent validity against a diagnostic interview for narcissistic personality disorder (NPD), but it does not explicitly define what a “diagnostic interview” is or that it is “used to determine whether a person meets the diagnosis.”

The packet supports that the diagnostic interview was used as a reference/criterion for comparing self-report screening measures, but the full definition’s general wording (“clinician-administered assessment,” and “whether a person meets the diagnosis”) is not explicitly stated in the provided text.

The packet supports a clinician-administered diagnostic interview for narcissistic personality disorder and its use as a comparison standard, but it does not support the broader claim that diagnostic interviews are used to determine whether a person meets the diagnosis for any particular mental disorder.
The definition generalizes from one study context (NPD) to the generic term without support from the packet.
